LESSON: POSITION AND SIZE OF COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and the Built Environments Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Afr
Topic 1.1: Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa, part of Natural and the Built Environments Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Afr in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we describe the position of countries in Eastern Africa? 2. How do we locate places on a map?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: A learner networking skill is developed as they use the internet and ICT tools with

assistive technology to play games on latitudes and longitudes and on sizes and positions of countries of Eastern

Africa.

● Communication and collaboration: A learner develop reading, writing, speaking, listening and teamwork skills when

brainstorming together with peers on the difference between latitudes and longitudes.

Values:
● Patriotism: A learner realizes their sense of identity as they sing the East African Community Anthem.

● Respect: A learner appreciates diverse opinions as they brainstorm in groups on the difference between latitudes and

longitudes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Critical Thinking skills: A Learner build their critical thinking skills as they brainstorm in groups on the

difference between latitudes and longitudes.

• Citizenship: A learner demonstrates patriotism as they sing the East African Community Anthem.

Link to other learning areas:

• Learners use Science and Technology knowledge when working with digital devices to locate positions of

countries in Eastern Africa based on their latitudes and longitudes.

• Learners apply Creative Arts skills to draw latitudes and longitudes on a sketch map of Eastern,

Suggested Learning Resources:

Maps of Eastern Africa, tactile maps of Eastern Africa, recorded computer games on latitudes and longitudes, digital devices

with assistive technology, approved appropriate print or braille Social Studies textbooks.
